rooms.title: Court of Three Trades
rooms.intro: Below the kiln, three lift bells wait in a dry cistern. Read the roll beside the survey lantern.

rooms.title: Archive of High Water
rooms.intro: An archivist filed the night of the flood by sound. Read the two surviving accounts, then play the four reliefs in the order the witnesses heard them.

rules.line: I was on the roof before the oar touched the gutter. The mill wheel was silent until the ferryman pulled us off.
First came the roof tiles giving way. The wheel began to turn after the oar struck. Only then did we hear Ina whistle through a reed.

rooms.title: Wrenfall Head
rooms.intro: Find Mirren at the chart shelter. A pilot cutter is waiting outside the reef.

rules.line: MIRREN  /  Tell the bell keeper who brought us in. All seven hands signed this page. Everyone who did the work gets a line.
MIRREN  /  Draw a triangle on my chart. West is the tide chapel. East is the split stone. The watcher on the north bluff can read the cutter’s last lamp.
MIRREN  /  The Linnet is carrying the last flood book. Her skipper can see our headland, but the guide lamps went out. Take my chart. I will meet her at the landing.
Three soundings make a safe entry. Read the brass rubbing in the western chapel, sight the two posts at Split Stone to the east, and climb the northern lookout. Then signal from the eastern mast.
A gull’s wing marks the full-flood line, above the drowned bell. Mirren’s cutter draws three fathoms. Open her passage with the WING flag.
A tide scale beside a worn footprint. The shore pilot can tell you whose draft to look for.

stations.label: Split Stone transit

rules.line: Look along the brass rail. The two ringed posts meet around the bell on the offshore rock. BELL is the second flag while the cutter crosses the bar.
Two rings frame a distant mark. Find Mirren in the chart shelter to learn the pilot code.

stations.direction: Look north along the brass rail. Center the gold bell beyond the two rings, then press E or trigger.

stations.label: North bluff glass

rules.line: Through the blue glass, the Linnet flashes the keeper’s star. STAR answers her and brings her into shelter. Raise the flags at the eastern mast.
Someone left the scope trained on a cutter. The shore pilot knows her call sign.

stations.direction: Face the cutter beyond the northern bluff. Center the star above her sail, then press E or trigger.

logEntry: Six salt-blurred names and Elin’s careful seventh. In the margin she wrote, “A bell can call for hands. It cannot promise on their behalf.”
logEndings: Elin has signed for the night tide. Six lines stand open for volunteers.
Ina opens the pilots’ book to the last page. “Do you think Elin would teach me to steer?”
